items.title: Devagar Que A Vida É Curta
Saints in The Wethouse
items.note: His debut album on XL, industrial rap collapsed into gothic synths and marching percussion, with dancehall guests and real intensity. Quiet moments like the acoustic "The Wind" cut through the chaos and give it weight.

items.title: Extraxxion
items.note: Debut album from Magu's KCR1 project, mixing bass, dub, gqom and changa with Afro-Venezuelan drums. Heavy, strange and physical.

items.title: Dizzy
items.note: Dear's return to Ghostly International, a sleazy, strutting electroclash single. Short, sharp and fun.

items.title: Devagar Que A Vida É Curta
items.note: Her second album, traditional Portuguese folk run through DAW-built electronics at full urgency, with tectonic percussion. A thrilling, defiant record about slowing down to actually live.

items.title: any1 can cook!
items.note: An Edinburgh producer's EP that moves fast between footwork, Jersey club, grime and baile funk without ever settling down. Restless, rough-edged club music.

items.title: Blackcurrant Jam
items.note: Sparse, jacking acid house from London's Mytron, from the Ascorbic EP. Lean and hypnotic, built for a late set.

items.title: Ma Waraa Al-Shaabi / Beyond Shaabi
items.note: Recorded in Iceland, his third solo album mixes high-BPM electronic dabke with slower drones and IDM textures. One foot in Levantine folk tradition, one in something far stranger.

items.title: Chapman's Pool
items.note: Will Dorey's one-man-band suite of breezy, lo-fi AM radio songs on a strong classic funk backbone, with some stranger detours. Easy to love, a little scuffed round the edges.

items.title: Snakes & Ladders
items.note: A surprise album about modern life lulling people into complacency, with jazz-leaning beats from Kenny Segal and others and plenty of gallows humour. billy woods and E L U C I D at their sharpest.

items.title: Warm Ground
items.note: Seven restrained, improvised guitar miniatures in under 18 minutes, with creaky doors and dropped mics worked into the texture. Small, warm and strange in the best way.

items.title: Snakes & Ladders
items.note: billy woods and ELUCID dropped this as a surprise on Backwoodz, with a different producer on every track. Pitchfork calls it intimate and close-up, with political and technological unease running through small, detailed sound worlds.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.artist: Anna Butterss, John Raymond, Ben Lumsdaine
items.title: Beginningless
items.note: Bass, horn and drums improvising live over two days in an LA studio, out on Northern Spy. Pitchfork hears it as spontaneous but grounded, and the trio name Jon Hassell as an influence.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Echo
items.note: His first solo album since 2019, about six years in the making and self-released on his own label. Pitchfork says it starts from cloud rap and wanders into pop rock, IDM and trip-hop.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Legendary Love
items.note: Her first full album since 2021, written around a two and a half year relationship. Warm production that leans on 80s and 90s R&B, with Nile Rodgers and Raphael Saadiq helping out.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Secret Language
items.note: The band's first full-length in 11 years, on Exploding in Sound. Pitchfork says it turns their usual inward-looking style toward parenthood, hobbies and grown-up responsibilities.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Trouble Mountain
items.note: Their first album together since 2021's Garbology, out on Rhymesayers. It's built around a ski resort fantasy set in the Poconos, with Blockhead on production.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Pirouette
items.note: A longer, more ambitious record than before. Pitchfork describes a pop and EDM base that pulls in emo, twee, ambient and choral music, with Mk.gee producing one track.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Year of the Rooster
items.note: The last of their Zodiac Cycle albums and the end of the Grass Can Move Stones trilogy, out on Tankcrimes with a lot of punk and rock guests. I couldn't find it on Spotify yet.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Dossier Scriptorium de Toulouse
items.note: The story of the Scriptorium de Toulouse, a type and calligraphy workshop that ran from 1967 to 2005 and trained a generation of French letter makers. Mostly unpublished documents and first-hand accounts, with contributions from nearly twenty type designers and calligraphers. 240 pages, two colour offset, French and English, designed by Juliette Flécheux with Bureau 205 and co-published with ANRT. A good one on how a school's way of teaching shapes the work that comes after it.

items.title: Some Other Book(i)s(h) Logos
items.note: 174 logos from small presses, zine makers, bookshops, book fairs and printers, all redrawn by hand by a third grader called Zaiah Drawing. It's a colouring book too, and the back of each fold gives the name, a short bio and the Instagram handle, so it doubles as a directory of the art book world. Designed by Kristen Mueller, coil bound, risograph and inkjet. Funny, and a sharp test of which marks survive being drawn by a child.

items.title: GraphicDesign.zip
items.note: Nearly a century of Swiss stamp design, looked at through eight lenses: format, shape, sheet layout, material, cropping, symbols, typography and imagery. Braille embossing, fabric stamps and foils turn up along the way. Tiny at 7.4 x 10.5 cm, 96 pages, Wire-O bound. Small screens are your world, and this is all about saying a lot in very little space.

items.title: Dreader Than Dreads: Posters by Fred Voisin
items.note: A folio of concert posters Frédéric Voisin made for reggae shows in Paris: Yellowman, Aswad, Culture, Burning Spear, Dennis Brown. Unbound, 16 pages, full colour, with a short text by Olivier Cachin. Published by le Signe, the national graphic design centre in Chaumont. This week's poster pick, and at $16 an easy one to say yes to.

items.title: PLOP #03: Polish Design Revue
items.note: A slim Polish design magazine asking what graphic design can do beyond selling or looking good. The theme is wrażliwość, roughly sensitivity or openness. Inside: Poster Rex's collective screen printing, Sonia Góral's family imagery, and Podpunkt's safety booklet that went to 16.8 million Polish households. 32 pages. Out in December.
items.by: Marian Misiak, Rene Wawrzkiewicz and Lars Harmsen

items.title: Mag to Mag Journal #2
items.note: The journal of Milan's independent magazine fair, run by the shop Frab's. This issue's theme is "Error", with interviews with MacGuffin's Ernst van der Hoeven, TypeOne's Amber Weaver and the Fukt team, plus a look at the Dutch distributor Idea Books. Big format, 160 pages, designed by Laura Bortolotti. A quick read on where indie magazines are now.

items.title: Fracture: Japanese Graphic Design 1875 to 1975
items.note: Not new (2024), but it fits well after the Japan books from earlier lists. Lynam traces Japanese graphic design from the graphic arts to just before digital, through essays on modernity, empire, gender, commerce and taste. 447 pages, hardback, from Set Margins'.

items.title: Graphic Design Play Book, Second Edition
items.note: Sophie Cure and Aurélien Farina teach type, signage, logos, posters and branding through puzzles: spot the difference, matching, dot to dot. Work by Otl Aicher, Otto Neurath and Gerd Arntz turns up along the way. Light, but handy for warming up a team workshop.

items.title: Meet the Lithographer
items.note: A picture book tour of a lithographer's workshop, from the invention of lithography to how books, posters and magazines get printed now. 40 pages, illustrations in three colours. Made for kids, but a clear, charming explainer at any age. Its sister book, Meet the Typographer, is there too.

items.title: Podpunkt
items.note: Warsaw branding studio behind the City of Warsaw logo, Culture.pl, the Adam Mickiewicz Institute and the Kraków National Museum, with a digital sister studio, Superskrypt, for UX and code. They also designed Poland's national safety guide. Public-facing design at real scale. Follow for identity systems that have to work for everyone.

items.title: H.D. Jean, 12oz Denim Indigo
items.note: Needles' exaggerated wide fit applied to a 5-pocket jean in 12oz denim. It has a worn-in vintage wash, darts and an adjustable waist cinch so you can pull the shape in.

items.title: Railroad Pant, Melange Double Cloth Brown
items.note: A roomy trouser based on old workwear, cut from a textured melange double cloth. Haven says it feels substantial but easy to wear every day.

items.title: Field Jacket, Cotton Ripstop Woodland
items.note: A military field jacket in woodland camo cotton ripstop. It has big gusseted chest pockets with flaps and adjustable cuffs, and the fabric is light enough to layer.

items.title: Between Snap Shirt, Poly Fleece Brown
items.note: A loose, unlined fleece shirt with a four-snap front and piped cuffs and hem. It works on its own or as a warm middle layer.

items.title: Watch Cap, Shetland Wool Umber
items.note: A ribbed beanie in Shetland wool, made in Japan. The only branding is a small purple butterfly embroidered on it.

items.title: W/N Wide Pants PT08263OS, Dark Brown
items.note: Wide trousers in a wool and nylon mix, made in Japan. The shop describes a lot of volume through the whole leg and a relaxed drape.

items.title: Wool Mixed Deep Tuck Pants PT07263OS, Black
items.note: Deep tucks give these extra room through the upper leg while the line stays clean. Cotton, wool and polyester, made in Japan.

items.title: Shoulder Stole GD04263OS, Melange Navy
items.note: A generous one-size stole in soft 100% wool, made in Japan. A simple way to add some texture to a plain outfit.

items.title: 101 Dad's Fit Denim Pant, Black Denim Stone
items.note: orSlow's relaxed Dad's Fit jean in soft stonewashed black denim, made in Japan. The shop notes the brand was started in 2005 by Ichiro Nakatsu, who studies old military and workwear.

items.title: Wave Cotton 85-252-006, Black
items.note: A loose long-sleeve crew in a wave-knit cotton with a bit of relief to the surface. It has dropped shoulders and is made in Japan by a knitwear company that runs much of its own production.

items.title: Balloon Wide Pants, Ash Grey
items.note: One of a run of new Beams trousers at Goodhood, in a soft ash grey. It sits alongside wide chinos, wide slacks and wide denim from the same drop, all well under £200.

items.title: Wide Denim Pants, Nep Indigo
items.note: Wide-leg Beams jeans in a nepped indigo denim, new at Goodhood this week. There is also a lighter Dusty Indigo version at the same price.

items.title: 3G Kasuri Nep Crew Neck Sweater, Olive
items.note: A chunky 3-gauge crew neck in a kasuri nep knit, new from Beams at Goodhood. Beams started in Harajuku in 1976, and this is one of the cheaper knits in the drop.

items.title: FISHERMAN-III Mock Neck, Terra Magma Brown
items.note: A fisherman-style mock neck knit from S.N.S. Herning, new in at Kyoto. It is the more affordable of the two Herning knits in this drop.

items.title: LOOSE 720, Dark Blue Vintage
items.note: The loose cut of jeans from Sunflower, a Copenhagen menswear label, in a dark vintage wash. Kyoto also has the slimmer Standard cut in the same wash.

items.title: 11oz Blue Denim Work Coat
items.note: A work coat in 11oz blue denim from Sugar Cane, new at Blue in Green. The SoHo shop is known for Japanese selvedge denim, and this arrived next to new Buzz Rickson's and orSlow pieces.

items.title: Original Spec. Chinos, Olive
items.note: Plain olive chinos from Buzz Rickson's, new at Blue in Green. The same drop has a pea coat and camo combat trousers, and at $170 these are the cheapest way in.

items.title: Vaquero Chambray Western Shirt, White
items.note: A western shirt in white chambray from Jelado, a Tokyo brand with a flagship in Ebisu. It is one of the newest things at Clutch Cafe, and there is a faded indigo denim version too.

items.title: Clutch Magazine Vol. 105: Made in Japan
items.note: The new issue of Clutch, the Tokyo men's style magazine, themed around things made in Japan. The London shop that sells it was set up by the magazine's editor, Atsushi Matsushima.

items.title: Sillage
items.note: A Tokyo label started by Nicolas Yuthanan Chalmeau, made in Japan. Its Circular Pants are very wide and come in one size, with an elastic drawstring waist. Blue in Green and Rendez-Vous both stock it now.
